title: How the build's sessions are organized: a coordinator per repo
why: Orchestrator, Oct 28 14:58 CDT: you proposed three tiers (coordinator, lane leads, triage, all Opus); an Opus blind review with web research says the shape is sound but the cut is wrong.
note: Home for the rulings: docs/decisions/session-tiers.md on main. One coordinator per repo; triage and a batch runner as standing sessions, started together by the coordinator before any lane, rotated before they go stale and archived only after draining; a session pushes back in one line when work reaches the wrong tier; shape is picked from the request (solo, one lane, coordinator). Rulings (shiv): item 50 b, lane sessions run Opus (Oct 28 16:15 CDT); item 53 a, a per-environment context window for cloud lanes, measured working Oct 28 17:53 CDT (lane read max_tokens 200000); item 59 a, keep today's helper-agent model table until a lane measures cost and quality (Oct 28 17:50 CDT); item 67 a, Opus grants live on the roadmap step (Oct 29 13:44 CDT; step opus-grant-on-step). Grant: "have just opus review building this out" (Oct 28 15:04 CDT). Built: L2 skills #794, L1 rules #797, L3 session-start #800 (batches 17 to 19). Left: item 59 a's measurement. Brief (coordinator's pick, Oct 30 03:56 CDT): over the next 5 lanes, compare tokens spent and review findings caught per lane, today's helper table against one step down, read from transcripts and PR reviews. Ready. Placed after c200 (triage 12, Oct 28). Arbiter (item 81 a, Oct 29 16:42 CDT): started only when shiv tells the coordinator "spawn arbiter", for long runs; high effort by default; its answers rule in its repo below his. #808, merged in batch 21 (1ce1fcb7).
